choices.why: The particles γὰρ and καὫ are coordinate intensifiers; ἄφθαρτον and ἀνώλεθρον are absolute negatives with privative alpha, best rendered as 'imperishable' and 'indestructible' to convey total immunity from decay and destruction.

Προσεπάγει is present active indicative third singular of προσεπíγνυμι, meaning 'to attach' or 'join to'; δὲ marks contrastive addition; τούτοις is dative plural referring to prior assertions. The sense is cumulative: he adds this demonstration to what was said before.

choices.english: a clear and most evident demonstration
choices.why: Σαφῆ and ἐναργεστάτην are accusative singular feminine agreeing with ἀπόδειξιν; ἐναργεστάτην is superlative of ἐναργής, meaning 'plainly visible' or 'evident to the senses'; the double adjective emphasizes both intellectual clarity and sensory certainty.
rejected: a plain and most visible proof

choices.term: Πρὸς τίνα γὰρ εἶπε τῶν ἀγγέλων Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου;
choices.english: 'To which of the angels did he ever say, Sit at my right hand?'
choices.why: This is a direct quotation from Psalm 110:1 (LXX), introduced by deliberative τίνα with γὰρ for emphasis; Κάθου is imperative second singular aorist of καθίζω; ἐκ δεξιῶν μου is ablative of source. The rhetorical question asserts no angel received this honor.
rejected: To which angel did he say

choices.why: Οὐχὶ expects negative answer; πάντες εἰσὶ is plural nominative of εἰμί; λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα is nominative plural neuter adjective with noun. The sense is that all angels are by nature servants, sent for service.

choices.term: εἰς διακονίαν ἀποστελλόμενα διὰ τοὺς μέλλοντας κληρονομεῖν σωτηρίαν
choices.english: sent forth for service because of those who are about to inherit salvation
choices.why: Εἰς διακονίαν indicates purpose; ἀποστελλόμενα is present passive participle neuter plural agreeing with πνεύματα; διὰ with accusative expresses causal agency; μέλλοντας κληρονομεῖν is present active participle accusative plural of μέλλω + κληρονομέω, future-in-past sense: 'those who are going to inherit'.
rejected: sent to serve those who will inherit salvation

choices.term: εἰ γὰρ ὁ μὲν τοῖς τῆς θεότητος ἐνί 382 δρυται θώκοις
choices.english: For if the one indeed partakes of the divine nature in trees
choices.why: This clause appears corrupted (τῆς θεότητος ἐνί 382 δρυται θώκοις); ἐνί may be OCR for ἐνί (dative of εἷς), 382 is likely a folio number misplaced, δρυται θώκοις seems like dryadsθώκοι (tree-dwellings). Despite corruption, the sense is participation in divinity through earthly symbols; we translate literally as fragments per instructions.
rejected: if he partakes of divinity in trees

choices.why: Τὸ δεσποτικὸν ἀξίωμα is accusative singular neuter of 'lordly dignity'; περικείμενος is present middle participle nominative singular of périekeimai, meaning 'lying around', 'surrounding'. The image is of dignity enveloping the subject.

choices.term: τίνι τῶν ὄντων ἀσυμφανὴς ἡ μεταξὺ κειμένη διαφορὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἀγγέλων
choices.english: to which of the existing things is the difference lying between Christ and angels invisible
choices.why: Τίνι is dative singular interrogative; τῶν ὄντων is genitive plural of ὤν, 'existing things'; ἀσυμφανὴς is nominative singular feminine of ἀσυμφανής, 'invisible'; ἡ μεταξὺ κειμένη διαφορὰ is 'the difference lying between'. The question asks where the invisible difference between Christ and angels resides among beings.
rejected: in which existing things is the difference between Christ and angels invisible

choices.term: οἱ δὲ τὸ δουλοπρεπὲς αὐχοῦσι μέτρον
choices.english: but the others, holding the servile measure
choices.why: Οἱ δὲ is nominative plural masculine contrasting with ὁ μὲν; τὸ δουλοπρεπὲς αὐχοῦσι is accusative singular neuter noun phrase with present active indicative third plural of αὐχέω, 'to hold', 'to carry'; μέτρον is 'measure', 'limit'. The angels possess only a measured, servile role.
rejected: but they pride themselves on servile measure

choices.term: καὶ πρὸς εὐκλείας τῆς ἀνωτάτω λελόγισται παρ' αὐτοῖς τὸ γνήσιον εἰς ὑπακοήν
choices.english: reckon the genuine to obedience toward the highest glory with them
choices.why: Πρὸς εὐκλείας τῆς ἀνωτάτω is genitive of price: 'for the highest glory'; λελόγισται is perfect middle indicative third singular of λογίζομαι, 'they reckon'; τὸ γνήσιον εἰς ὑπακοήν is accusative 'the genuine unto obedience'. The angels consider true worth to lie in obedience, not innate glory.
rejected: they count the genuine as obedience to the highest glory

choices.term: ἀντακούσεται παρ' ἡμῶν ὡς εἴπερ ἕλοιτο τὴν τῆς ἀληθοῦς ἑνώσεως ἐννοῆσαι δύναμιν
choices.english: he will receive back from us as if he had chosen to conceive the power of the true union
choices.why: ἀντακούσεται is future middle indicative third singular of ἀντακούομαι, 'to receive in return'; παρ' ἡμῶν is ablative 'from us'; ὡς εἴπερ ἕλοιτο is comparative condition: 'as if he should choose'; τὴν τῆς ἀληθοῦς ἑνώσεως ἐννοῆσαι δύναμιν is accusative 'the power to conceive the true union'. The rebuttal imagines the opponent imagining Christ's power as merely conceptual.
rejected: he will get back from us as if he wanted to imagine the power of true union

pass_b_english: For indeed, with him nothing is imperishable and indestructible. Moreover, he adds to these points a clear and most evident demonstration of his natural superiority, quoting Scripture: 'To which of the angels did he ever say, Sit at my right hand?' Are not all spirits ministering, sent forth for service on account of those who are about to inherit salvation? For if one who partakes of the divine nature—even if imagined as surrounded by lordly dignity, even if conceived as son of David having taken a body from the holy virgin—yet those who stand present as God and king of all things, to which of the existing beings is the difference lying between Christ and angels invisible? For the one indeed is Son and God, but the others, holding only the measure of servility, reckon that genuine worth consists in obedience to the highest glory; they consider the true to be found in submission, not in innate honor.

But if anyone should say, And who will persuade us in what way one might think him, having been born in the last times of the age through the holy virgin, to have founded the earth at the beginning and themselves to have raised up the heavens, he will receive back from us as if he had chosen to conceive the power of the true union—not the union understood merely in distinct persons or according to will and good pleasure—he will indeed find, through the economy of God, that the human things have come to pass, and that they are not foreign to the divine purpose.
